INSTRUCTIONS SEE OVER

FORM NO. 3
G. 50M-1/27
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.1, Special Branch established,
REPORT
Date Sept. 12, 1940.
Subject (in full) Lists of Radio Stations in Shanghai.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan
Attached herewith are four lists of radio
stations operating in Shanghai :-
(a) List of Amateur Shortwave Radio Stations.
(b) List of Commercial Shortwave Radio Stations.
(c) List of Commercial Broadcasting Stations.
(d) List of Broadcasting Stations engaged in
broadcasting news and comments.
FILE
Logan
D. S. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)
（批：Sent, 13/9.）

日期 1940年9月12日。
主题（全称）上海无线电台列表。
由副督察长洛根（Logan）制作并呈送
随函附上四份在上海运营的无线电台列表：-
(a) 业余短波无线电台列表。
(b) 商业短波无线电台列表。
(c) 商业广播电台列表。
(d) 从事新闻和评论广播的广播电台列表。

S. B. REGISTRY

Date October 20. 1939
Subject List of Short Wave Stations in Shanghai
Made by. D.S.I. McAdie Forarded by. C. Guesst
Attached is an up to date list giving
particulars of known short wave radio stations in
Shanghai, including call signs, power, wavelength
etc.
The control station denotes the place where
the actual messages are tipped out whence they
may be conveyed by telephone wire to the transmitter.
As the control stations also receive messages the
separation from the transmitters is done to prevent
interference which would be experienced close to
sets with a large power output.

03577
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY. H. D. 6813/
APR 4 1939
Nipponese Preparing
Canton Broadcasting
In Chinese, English
(Reuter's Agency)
CANTON, Apr. 4.—With all pre-
parations nearing completion, the
Japanese authorities here expect to
begin broadcasting from Canton
in the near future, probably with-
in a week.
The call-sign of the station
which is said to be practically
ready, will be. HDOK, and all
broadcasts will be on short waves
According to a tentative pro-
ram, broadcasts will be made in
English and Chinese, and will in-
clude lectures, news—foreign, local
and on the Sino-Japanese war—
and musical recordings.
page_data.zh:
03577
《上海晚邮报与信使报》。H. D. 6813/
1939年4月4日
日本人准备
在广州进行广播
使用中文、英文
（路透社）
广州，4月4日电。——随着各项准备工作接近完成，此间的日本当局预计不久将开始从广州进行广播，可能在一周之内。
据称该电台已基本就绪，其呼号为 HDOK，所有广播均使用短波。
根据暂定节目单，广播将使用英语和汉语，内容包括讲座、新闻（国际、本地及中日战争相关新闻）以及音乐唱片录音。

page_data.en:
02851
REGIS
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
MAR 1 6 1939

Chungking to Broadcast
To World
New Radio Station Opened;
British Installation
Chungking, Mar. 14.
The Central Broadcasting Station
here has officially announced the
commencement of broadcasts over a
new 35-kilowatt shortwave station,
for Britain, France, Italy, Germany,
North America, Siberia, Manchuria,
North China, Japan, the South Seas
and Soviet Russia.
The new powerful station was con-
structed by the British concern of
Marconi's Wireless Telegraph Com-
pany Ltd.
It was originally intended for Nan-
king, but after the commencement of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities, it was
moved to Chungking.
Special broadcasts for Britain,
under the call sign of XGOY, operat-
ing on a wave-length of 25.51 metres,
will be made daily at 11 p.m. London
time. It will consist of daily new
bulletins.—Reuter.
page_data.zh:
02851
REGIS
《字林西报》，
1939年3月16日

重庆向全世界广播
新电台开通；
英国安装设备
重庆，3月14日。
此间的中央广播电台已正式宣布，通过一座新的35千瓦短波电台开始广播，覆盖英国、法国、意大利、德国、北美、西伯利亚、满洲、华北、日本、南洋群岛及苏维埃俄罗斯。
这座新的强力电台由英国马可尼无线电报有限公司（Marconi's Wireless Telegraph Company Ltd.）承建。
该台原计划设于南京，但在中日敌对行动开始后，迁至重庆。
对英国的特别广播，呼号为 XGOY，工作波长为25.51米，将于伦敦时间每晚11点播出。内容将为每日新闻简报。——路透社。

of short wave as

at me on more than one

Herb Robertson
D.C. Special Branch.
page_data.zh:
备忘录。
1930年1月6日
警务处长助理致警务处处长。

提供共产党电台清单是合乎规定的，
但出于显而易见的原因，
我反对从警察总部发出任何短波电台清单
（即使是发给秘书处），
因为日本人已多次向我索要此类信息。

Herb Robertson
特别处副督察长。

30 12 38）

23rd December, 1938.

Sir,

I have been approached by a publishing
firm in New Zealand to furnish them with an up-
to-date list of Broadcast and Shortwave Stations
in China.

In the disturbed conditions at present
existing throughout this country I fully realise
that it is not possible to furnish the information
required with any degree of accuracy, but I should
be very grateful if you could let me have a list
of such stations at present operating in that part
of Shanghai administered by your Council, their
frequencies and operating power, if such a list is
available.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(sgd) A. H. George

COMMERCIAL COUNSELLOR

The Secretary,
The Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

TRANSLATION OF FRENCH POLICE REPORT NO. 1752/S DATED 30.4.1937.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

SUBJECT:    1) RADIO BROADCASTING IN CHINA.
            2) CHARACTERISTICS AND LOCATIONS OF THE PRINCIPAL
               RADIO BROADCASTING STATIONS IN THE FAR EAST.

1.  RADIO BROADCASTING IN CHINA  -  ORGANISATION OF.
        In December 1932 China took part in the International
Conference held in Madrid.  The Conference decided to adopt
the "General Regulations concerning radio communication."
        According to the contents of these regulations, frequencies
assigned to all fixed, land and broadcasting stations, as well as
their power limits must be made known to the Bureau of the Union
for publication purposes, in order that the stations concerned
may conduct regular services and avoid causing international
interference.    Frequencies must be chosen in such a manner to
avoid, as far as possible, interfering with international services
belonging to countries that are members of the Union and conducted
or operated by existing stations, the frequencies of which have
already been notified to the Union.    The above notification must
be made prior to the service being operated and sufficient time
must be given to allow the various administrations to take such
steps that they deem necessary for the efficient functioning of
their own services.
        In principle, the power of radio broadcasting stations
must not exceed that limit that will permit of an economic but
efficient national service of good quality within the boundaries
of the countries concerned.
        The location of powerful radio broadcasting stations, and
more particularly of those working near these frequency bands re-
served for broadcasting, must be selected in such a way to avoid
as much as possible, causing interference with broadcasting ser-
vices of other countries or to other services operating on nearly
similar frequencies.

1937年4月30日第1752/S号法国警察报告译文。
------------------------------------------------------------------------

主题：    1) 中国的无线电广播。
            2) 远东主要无线电广播电台的特征及位置。

1.  中国的无线电广播 - 组织情况。
        1932年12月，中国参加了在马德里举行的国际会议。会议决定通过《关于无线电通信的一般规章》。
        根据这些规章的内容，分配给所有固定台、陆地台和广播电台的频率及其功率限制必须告知联盟局以便公布，从而使有关电台能够开展正常业务并避免造成国际干扰。选择频率的方式必须尽可能避免干扰属于联盟成员国的国际业务，以及由现有电台开展或运营的业务，这些电台的频率已通知联盟。上述通知必须在业务运营之前发出，并留出足够的时间，以便各管理部门采取其认为必要的措施，以确保其自身业务的有效运行。
        原则上，无线电广播电台的功率不得超过在有关国家境内提供经济但高效且高质量的国内服务所允许的限度。
        大功率无线电广播电台的位置，特别是那些在预留用于广播的频段附近工作的电台，其选址方式应尽可能避免对其他国家的广播服务或在非常相近的频率上运行的其他服务造成干扰。

The administrations of the contracting countries may,
under reserve of the contents of the above mentioned paragraphs,
assign any frequency and any type of wave to any radio station
under their authority, on condition that they do not result in
interference with other countries' services.

China has been assigned thirty-one frequency bands
by the Radiocommunications International Consulting Committee
(See Appendix I - Official Schedule of frequencies assigned
to China). In reality, however, China possesses only three
stations the power of which exceeds 10 kilowatts and which
might possibly cause interference with international commun-
ications. (See Appendix II - List of radio stations at present
operating in China).

Chinese radio broadcasting stations are divided into
four categories or systems:

1. Stations dependent on the Minister of Communications.
2. Stations dependent on the Nanking Central Tangpu.
3. Stations dependent on Provincial or Municipal Governments.
4. Private Stations.

The first three categories are responsible directly
or indirectly to the Central Authorities, transmitting ident-
ical programmes in which Chinese politics and the education of
the masses play the greater part. They are subsidised by
the Central Government (Minister of Communications) and by the
Provincial Governments.

SITUATION ON JANUARY 1, 1936.

Up till December 1935 private radio broadcasting
stations were not subject to the control of the Central Auth-
orities. Provisional Regulations, which are still in force,
governed them (See Appendix III).

Since that time the Central Government has become
very anxious regarding the great freedom accorded to private
stations. Control bureaux have been set up in the prin-
cipal towns in China (Shanghai, Nanking, Tientsin, Peiping,

各缔约国政府，在保留上述段落内容的前提下，可向在其管辖下的任何无线电台分配任何频率和任何类型的波段，条件是不致对其他国家的业务造成干扰。

国际无线电咨询委员会已为中国分配了三十一个频段（参见附录一——分配给中国的官方频率表）。然而实际上，中国目前仅有三个功率超过10千瓦的电台，这些电台可能会对国际通信造成干扰。（参见附录二——中国目前运营的无线电台列表）。

中国的无线广播电台分为四类或四个系统：

1. 隶属于交通部的电台。
2. 隶属于南京中央党部的电台。
3. 隶属于省或市政府的电台。
4. 私营电台。

前三类电台直接或间接向中央当局负责，播放相同的节目，其中中国政治和民众教育占据主要部分。它们由中央政府（交通部）和省政府提供补贴。

1936年1月1日的情况。

直到1935年12月，私营无线广播电台不受中央当局的管制。当时适用的是暂行条例，该条例至今仍然有效（参见附录三）。

自那时以来，中央政府对于给予私营电台的巨大自由变得非常担忧。在中国的主要城市（上海、南京、天津、北平、

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Hankow, Canton, etc). These control bureaux have it as
a duty to bring to the notice of the Minister of Commun-
ications all the faults of the stations under their control.
In accordance with Article XXV of the Provisional Regu-
lations, the Minister of Communications may cancel those
licences issued to stations for infringements.

In 1936 (November), a Broadcasting Central Commit-
tee was created, the head office of which is situated in
Nanking. New restrictions concerning private radio stat-
ions were adopted. They tend to make Chinese broadcast-
ing a means of cultural instruction (See Appendix IV -
Time Schedule for Broadcasts from Private Radio Stations).

The Central Government, however, is running counter
to the interests of the owners of private stations, for
the hours set apart for the transmission of educational
programmes obtain the greater part of their revenues.
From 8 p.m. until 9.5 p.m for example, private stations
must re-transmit the programmes broadcast by the central
station in Nanking: now this hour is the most remuner-
ative for the transmission of advertising announcements.

REMARKS.

Following the example of other powers, China is
obviously attempting to bring its broadcasting system under
state control. In Shanghai, in particular, a certain
number of private stations will be closed down during 1937.

A statute on Chinese radio broadcasting is now
in the process of being prepared in Nanking. It will be
promulgated in several months' time.

汉口、广州等）设立了管制局。这些管制局的职责是将其管辖下电台的所有违规行为报告给交通部部长。根据《暂行条例》第二十五条，交通部部长可因违规行为撤销发给电台的执照。

1936年（11月），成立了广播中央委员会，其总部设在南京。针对私营无线电台采取了新的限制措施。这些措施旨在使中国的广播成为文化教导的手段（参见附录四——私营无线电台广播时间表）。

然而，中央政府的作法与私营电台业主的利益相悖，因为用于播放教育节目的时段占据了他们收入的大部分。例如，从晚上8点到9点5分，私营电台必须重播南京中央台播出的节目：而这一小时本是播放广告公告最有利可图的时段。

备注。

效仿其他列强的做法，中国显然正试图将其广播系统置于国家控制之下。特别是在上海，一定数量的私营电台将在1937年期间被关闭。

一部关于中国无线广播的法令目前正在南京起草中。它将在几个月后颁布。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX III

TRANSLATION

Provisional Regulations Controlling Private
Radio Stations

Article I - Any station which by means of radiophonic trans-
mitters, transmits speech or music, shall be known as a
Radio Broadcasting Station. Radio Broadcasting Stations
must be equipped and used in accordance with these present
regulations.

Article II - Any citizen of the Republic of China, any com-
pany or society wholly Chinese, any school or any association
registered with the National Government or any lawfully
established corporation may set up radio broadcasting stations
in Chinese territory. But the installation may only be made
after a permit has been issued by the Minister of Commun-
ications. In the case of a Company or an Association, part
of whose capital has not been subscribed by Chinese, wishing
to set up a radio station, this Society or Association may
only request the issue of this permit and set up radio
broadcasting stations in Chinese territory, after it has
registered with the Chinese National Government and has
obtained a registration certificate.

Article III - When a request is made for the issue of a
permit for the erection of a radio broadcasting station,
the responsible representative must fill in clearly the
following:

1. Name of the society or association, details of its
organisation, its address and full name of the chief
of the station.

2. Object of establishing the radio station.

3. Name of the radio station to be created, details of
its organisation and an estimate of expenses.

4. Power of transmitting apparatus, location of this
apparatus and details of the work projected (details
must be accompanied by a rough plan).

5. Location of the studio.

Article IV - Requests for the issue of a permit must be
accompanied by $10 (permit fee) and $1 (stamp tax).

Article V - The permit is valid for six months, after
which it will be considered as null and useless. If,
for some particular reason, the radio station cannot be
completed within the stipulated time, the interested party
may, one month prior to the expiration of the stipulated
time, explain the reasons to the Minister of Communications
and request him to prolong the period for three months.
Only one extension period will be permitted.

Article VI - After the installation of the radio station has
been completed, the Minister of Communications will only issue
the licence after an examination of the station by a delegate
sent by him. The delegate will examine the works, apparatus
and installations and will see that they are in good condition.
page_data.zh:
附录三

译文

管理私人无线电台暂行条例

第一条 - 凡利用无线电发射机传送语音或音乐的电台，均称为无线电广播电台。无线电广播电台必须按照本条例的规定配备和使用。

第二条 - 中华民国公民、 wholly Chinese（全华资）公司或社团、在国民政府注册的学校或协会，或依法成立的公司，均可在中国领土内设立无线电广播电台。但须在交通部部长颁发许可证后方可安装。若公司或协会的部分资本非由华人认购，欲设立无线电台，该社团或协会须先在中华民国国民政府注册并取得注册证书后，方可申请颁发此许可证并在中国领土内设立无线电广播电台。

第三条 - 申请颁发设立无线电广播电台许可证时，负责人必须清楚填写以下内容：

1. 社团或协会名称、其组织详情、地址及台长全名。

2. 设立电台的目的。

3. 拟设电台的名称、其组织详情及费用估算。

4. 发射设备的功率、设备位置及工程计划详情（详情须附草图）。

5. 播音室位置。

第四条 - 申请颁发许可证须附带10美元（许可证费）和1美元（印花税）。

第五条 - 许可证有效期为六个月，逾期视为无效。若因特殊原因，电台无法在规定期限内完工，利害关系人可在规定期限届满前一个月，向交通部部长说明理由，并请求延长三个月。仅允许延期一次。

第六条 - 电台安装完成后，交通部部长将在其派出的代表对电台进行检查后，方予颁发执照。代表将检查工程、设备及安装情况，并确保其状况良好。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX III - Page 2.

At the same time, the interested party will return to the
Minister of Communications the permit previously obtained.

Article VII - The request for the issue of the licence must
be accompanied by $50 (licence fee), $2 (stamp tax) and a
deposit of $200 or a shop security amounting $1,000. The
security - or the amount of the security - will be reimburs-
able.

Article VIII - After the publication of definite Regulations,
the licence must be renewed.

Article IX - If a licence is lost or theinterested party
changes the details mentioned in this licence, he must inform
the Minister of Communications and request him, within one
wekk, to issue a duplicate of the licence or a new licence
after having explained the reasons for his request.

Article X - A request for the issue of a duplicate licence
or a new licence must be accompanied by the licence fee and
stamp tax fee as provided for in Article VII. If, however,
the change in the licence is ordered by the Minister of
Communications, the interested party shall be exonerated
(from payment).

Article XI - Radio broadcasting station licences are not
transferable and must not be lent or hired.

Article XII - The call signs of radio broadcasting stations
will be arranged by the Minister of Communications.

Article XIII - The frequencies of radio broadcasting stations
must be arranged by the Minister of Communications and must
be continually checked and regulated in order that they do
not exceed the arranged frequency by more than 0.2%.

Article XIV - It is necessary as much as possible to reduce
the power of the harmonic waves from antennae, in order to
avoid causing interference with other radio broadcast stat-
ions. If these waves are too strong, the Minister of Com-
munications may order the interested station to reduce them
(i.e. to improve them), or again to cease transmitting its
programme.

Article XV - During the course of programmes, the call sign
and frequency must be given each thirty minutes.

Article XVI - In case of necessity, the Minister of Commun-
ications may at any time modify the licence conditions as
he may deem fit as well as the contents of articles X and XI.

Article XVII - Transmissions over radio stations are limited
to the following:

1. Talks of public interest.
2. Press news. (In case of necessity the Minister of Com-
munications may censor such news).
3. Music, songs and other amusement programmes.
4. Commercial information (The time allowed this item must
not exceed one-fifth of the time employed by a radio
station in its daily broadcasts and transmissions).
page_data.zh:
附录三 - 第2页。

同时，利害关系人须将此前获得的许可证交还交通部部长。

第七条 - 申请颁发执照须附带50美元（执照费）、2美元（印花税）以及200美元保证金或价值1,000美元的店铺担保。该保证金——或担保金额——可予退还。

第八条 - 在正式条例公布后，执照必须续期。

第九条 - 若执照遗失，或利害关系人变更执照中提及的细节，必须通知交通部部长，并在说明申请理由后，于一周内请求补发执照副本或新执照。

第十条 - 申请补发执照副本或新执照，须附带第七条规定的执照费和印花税。但是，若执照的变更是由交通部部长命令进行的，则免除利害关系人的缴费义务。

第十一条 - 无线电广播电台执照不得转让，不得出借或出租。

第十二条 - 无线电广播电台的呼号由交通部部长安排。

第十三条 - 无线电广播电台的频率由交通部部长安排，并须不断检查和调节，以确保其不超过规定频率的0.2%。

第十四条 - 须尽可能降低天线谐波功率，以避免对其他无线电广播电台造成干扰。若这些谐波过强，交通部部长可命令相关电台降低谐波（即进行改进），或停止播放其节目。

第十五条 - 在节目播出过程中，每三十分钟必须播报呼号和频率。

第十六条 - 如有必要，交通部部长可随时修改其认为合适的执照条件，以及第十条和第十一条的内容。

第十七条 - 无线电台的传输内容限于以下各项：

1. 公共利益谈话。
2. 新闻。（如有必要，交通部部长可审查此类新闻）。
3. 音乐、歌曲及其他娱乐节目。
4. 商业信息（此项所占时间不得超过电台每日广播和传输所用时间的五分之一）。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX III - Page 3.

Article XVIII - The Minister of Communications reserves the
right to broadcast over radio stations decrees, orders, news,
proclamations emanating from Government Administration sources,
as well as propaganda talks. If such decrees, orders, etc...
......are sufficiently important, he may also have them
transmitted by these stations (prior to other talks, news, eetc.
......)

Article XIX - If, in case of accident, a radio transmitting
station located on a ship or an aeroplane requests help, and
a radio broadcasting station hears the S.O.S. or is informed
of it by a maritime or land radio station under the control
of the Minister of Communications, it must cease transmitting
in order to avoid interference and to save or obviate any
disaster. The radio broadcasting station in question may only
recommence its transmissions after requests for help have
ceased.

Article XX - Any radio broadcasting station that has not
obtained from the Minister of Communications the necessary
licence, or who is in possession of a cancelled licence, or
who has not yet requested a duplicate for a licence already
lost, has no right to transmit broadcasts.

Article XXI - The Minister of Communications may at any time
despatch inspectors to examine the documents, books, and
important schedules of radio broadcasting stations and the
work carried out by them. The stations concerned shall
not, under any pretext whatever, refuse access to the
inspectors in question.

Article XXII - Stations are forbidden to:

1. To cause interference or do anything prejudicial to radio
stations belonging to the State, Navy, Army, Air Force
and the public.

2. To refuse to be guided and controlled by the inspectors
of the Minister of Communications.

3. To communicate with other stations for the purpose of
transmitting news.

4. To transmit unreliable news and information.

5. To transmit news of a personal nature.

6. To transmit words, news, songs, literary works of such
nature as to cause a breach of the peace or corrupt
good morals.

7. To cause interference with other stations whilst they are
functioning.

Article XXIII - The International Convention of Radiotelegraphy
and its appendix are applicable to radio broadcasting stations
when they are in agreement with these stations and are not in
opposition to the present regulations.

Article XXIV - The laws and decrees concerning radiography
published by the Minister of Communications of the National
Government as well as the various provisional regulations
regarding radiography are applicable to radio broadcasting
stations when they are in accord with these stations and are
not in opposition to the present regulations.
page_data.zh:
附录三 - 第3页。

第十八条 - 交通部部长保留通过无线电广播电台广播源自政府行政部门的法令、命令、新闻、公告以及宣传谈话的权利。若此类法令、命令等……足够重要，他也可命令通过这些电台优先于其他谈话、新闻等进行传输。

第十九条 - 若遇事故，位于船舶或飞机上的无线电发射台请求援助，且无线电广播电台听到S.O.S.信号，或经由交通部部长管辖下的海上或陆地无线电台获知此信号，必须停止发射，以避免干扰并挽救或避免任何灾难。相关无线电广播电台仅在求助信号停止后，方可重新开始传输。

第二十条 - 任何未从交通部部长处获得必要执照，或持有已注销执照，或执照遗失后尚未申请补发的无线电广播电台，无权进行广播传输。

第二十一条 - 交通部部长可随时派遣视察员检查无线电广播电台的文件、簿册、重要时间表及其开展的工作。相关电台不得以任何借口拒绝上述视察员进入。

第二十二条 - 禁止电台从事以下行为：

1. 对属于国家、海军、陆军、空军及公众的无线电台造成干扰或做任何有害之事。

2. 拒绝接受交通部视察员的指导和控制。

3. 为传输新闻目的与其他电台通信。

4. 传输不可靠的新闻和信息。

5. 传输个人性质的新闻。

6. 传输可能导致破坏和平或败坏良好道德的言论、新闻、歌曲、文学作品。

7. 在其他电台运作时造成干扰。

第二十三条 - 《国际无线电报公约》及其附录适用于无线电广播电台，前提是它们与这些电台相符且不违背本条例。

第二十四条 - 国民政府交通部部长发布的有关无线电报的法律和法令，以及有关无线电报的各项暂行条例，适用于无线电广播电台，前提是它们与这些电台相符且不违背本条例。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX III - Page 4.

Article XXV - Any infraction of any of the articles of
the present regulations will be liable, according to the
gravity of the case, to any of the following penalties:

1. Cessation of transmitting broadcasts.

2. Cancellation of the licence.

3. Confiscation of the apparatus and a fine of from
$50 to $2,000.

Article XXVI - In the event of a radio broadcasting
station infringing any of the present regulations, its
Chief will be held responsible.

Article XXVII - The Minister of Communications may at any
time revise the present regulations and publish the revised
regulations.

Article XXVIII - The present regulations will go into
effect as from the date of their publication.
page_data.zh:
附录三 - 第4页。

第二十五条 - 违反本条例任何条款者，视情节轻重，须承担以下任一处罚：

1. 停止广播传输。

2. 吊销执照。

3. 没收设备并处以50至2,000美元罚款。

第二十六条 - 若无线电广播电台违反本条例任何规定，其台长须承担责任。

第二十七条 - 交通部部长可随时修订本条例并公布修订后的条例。

第二十八条 - 本条例自公布之日起生效。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX IV - Page 3.

Details regarding Provisional Time Schedule for Broad-
casts from Private Radio Stations.

1. The duration of broadcasts from private radio stations will
be in accordance with the power of these stations. Daily,
the broadcasting periods will be:-
a. 10 hours for stations of less that 50 W. Power.
b. 12 hours for stations of between 50 W. and 1,000 W. power.
c. 15 hours for stations of between 1,000 W. and 10,000 W.
power.

2. No station may broadcast for a period of less than 5 hours.

3. Broadcasting is only permitted between 6 a.m. and midnight,
except on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, when broadcasting
will be permitted for one hour only during the mornings.
Radio stations must broadcast didactic and amusement programmes
at the times stated on the attached schedule.

4. Schedule No. 1 is the main schedule:, schedules Nos. 2, 3, 4
and 5 are additional. Each schedule gives the type of pro-
gramme to be broadcast during a period of 12 hours. Each
station will choose that schedule that is most convenient
to its own needs.
For programmes of less than 12 hours duration, and those on
Sundays and holidays, stations will be able to reduce the
number of broadcast hours in accordance with the schedule
of which they make use.

5. Any radio station may commence its transmission before or after
the opening hour on the programme, but it must broadcast the
best parts of this programme. For example, a station commences
its transmission at 8 a.m., whilst the schedule allows for
stories, songs, etc. from 7.30 a.m. until 8.10 a.m. Thus
the station has not more than 10 minutes in which to broadcast
a selection of the scheduled programme.
Radio stations must not interrupt their programmes or trans-
missions; a temporary halt in transmitting is only permitted
after two consecutive hours of transmission.
page_data.zh:
附录四 - 第3页。

关于私营广播电台临时广播时间表的细则。

1. 私营广播电台的广播时长将根据这些电台的功率而定。每日广播时段如下：
a. 功率低于50瓦的电台为10小时。
b. 功率在50瓦至1,000瓦之间的电台为12小时。
c. 功率在1,000瓦至10,000瓦之间的电台为15小时。

2. 任何电台的广播时间不得少于5小时。

3. 除星期六、星期日和节假日外，仅允许在上午6时至午夜之间进行广播；在星期六、星期日和节假日，仅允许在上午广播一小时。广播电台必须按照附表规定的时间播出教化和娱乐节目。

4. 时间表1为主时间表；时间表2、3、4和5为附加时间表。每个时间表列出了12小时内应播出的节目类型。各电台可根据自身需要选择最方便的时间表。
对于不足12小时的节目，以及星期日和节假日的节目，各电台可根据其所使用的时间表减少广播小时数。

5. 任何广播电台可在节目规定的开始时间之前或之后开始传输，但必须播出该节目中最精彩的部分。例如，某电台于上午8时开始传输，而时间表允许在上午7时30分至8时10分播出故事、歌曲等。因此，该电台只有不超过10分钟的时间来播出预定节目中的选段。
广播电台不得中断其节目或传输；仅在连续传输两小时后，才允许暂时停止传输。

page_data.en:
APPENDIX IV - Page 4.

6. Broadcasts on economic, weather and news bulletins, the
duration of which exceeds five minutes, will be given during
those times reserved for didactic transmissions; those of
less than five minutes may be given during those periods
reserved for amusement programmes.

7. When didactic broadcasts are not finished at the correct time,
they may be prolonged by infringing into those periods
reserved for recreation or amusement programmes.
The inverse of this may not be carried out.

8. Advertising broadcasts will have the same 'character' schedule
heading as the transmission which it replaces.

9. Advertising will only be given during amusement transmission
periods.

10. Religious matters will be included in the didactic programme.
Their transmission will not exceed one-half of the time
reserved for the didactic programme. If this is not suf-
ficient, it will be continued in the amusement period,
without, however, exceeding one-half of this latter period.

11. The duration of talks, songs and music in the Shanghai and
Soochow dialects, jokes, Yangchow songs, Yangchow and Ningpo
modern theatres, Ningpo songs, may not exceed two hours daily.

12. Broadcasts will be divided as follows: 38% for educational
programmes and 68% for amusement.
Broadcasts on economic, weather and news matters, etc....
will be given during those period reserved for amusement.

13. Tests will be made at the following times:
Midnight to 2 a.m., 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
Part programmes will be sent over the air.

14. Short-wave radio stations are not compelled to keep to the
times mentioned in the schedule.

15. Broadcasts of ceremonies, sports meetings, festivals, etc...
will take place during the times reserved for tests; owners
of private stations interested in such broadcasts will request
permission from our Committee.

Drawn up by the Radiobroadcast
Central Committee.
page_data.zh:
附录四 - 第4页。

6. 时长超过五分钟的经济、天气和新闻简报广播，将在预留用于教化传输的时段内播出；时长少于五分钟的，可在预留用于娱乐节目的时段内播出。

7. 当教化广播未能在正确时间结束时，可占用预留用于休闲或娱乐节目的时段予以延长。反之则不可行。

8. 广告广播将与其所替代的传输具有相同的“性质”时间表标题。

9. 广告仅在娱乐传输时段内播出。

10. 宗教事项将包含在教化节目中。其传输时间不得超过预留给教化节目时间的一半。如果这不够用，可在娱乐时段继续，但不得超过该娱乐时段的一半。

11. 上海话和苏州话的演讲、歌曲和音乐，笑话，扬州小曲，扬州和宁波的现代戏剧，宁波歌曲，每日总时长不得超过两小时。

12. 广播分配如下：38%用于教育节目，68%用于娱乐。
有关经济、天气和新闻等事项的广播……将在预留给娱乐的时段内播出。

13. 测试将在以下时间进行：
午夜至凌晨2时，上午10时至11时，以及下午2时至4时。
部分节目将通过空中发送。

14. 短波广播电台不必遵守时间表中提到的时间。

15. 仪式、运动会、节日等的广播将在预留给测试的时段内进行；对此类广播感兴趣的私营电台业主需向本委员会申请许可。

由无线电广播中央委员会制定。

1. HADIO SROADCASTING IN CHINA - ORGANISATION OF. 
in December 1932 China took part in the international 


Conference held in Madrid. The Conference decided to adopt 
the “General Regulations concerning radio communication.® 

According to the contents of these regulations, frequencies 
assigned to all fixed, land and broadcasting stations, asxwell as 

their power limits must be made known to the sureau of the Union 
for publication purposes, in order that the stations concerned 
may conduct regular services and avoid causing international 
interference. Frequencies must be chosen in sueh a manner te 
avoid, ae far as possible, interfering with intermatieonal services 
belonging to countries that are members of the Union and conducted 
or operated by existing stations, the frequencies of which have 
already been notified to the Union. The above notification must 
be made prior to the service being operated and sufficient time 
must be given to allow the various administrations to take sueh 
steps that they deem necessary for the efficient functioning of 
their own services. 

In principle, the power of radio broadcasting stations 
must not exoeed that limit that will permit of an economic but 
efficient national service of good quality within the boundaries 
of the countries concerned. 

the location of powerful radio broadcasting stations, and 
more particularly of those working near these frequeney Bands re- 
served for breadcasting, must be selected in eueh a way te avoid 
as much as possible, eausing interferesee with broadcasting sere 
vices of other countries or to ether services eperating eon nearly 
similar frequeneios.

The administrations of the contracting countries may, 
under reserve of the contents of the above mentioned paragraphs, 
assign any frequency and any type of wave to any radio station 
under their uuthority, on condition that they do not result in 
interference with other countries’ services. 

China has been assigned thirty-one #reyuency bands 
by the Radiocommunications International Consulting Committee 
(See Appemdix I - Official Schedule of frequencies assigned 
to China). In reality, however, China possesses only three 
stations the power of which exceeds 10 kilowatts and which 
might possibly cause interefence with international commun= 
ications. (See Appendix II - List of radio stations at present 
operating in China). 

Chinese radio brosaacasting stations are divided into 
four categories or systems: 

1. . Stations dependent on the Minister of Communications. 

2. Stations dependent on the Nanking Central Tangpu. 

3. Stations dependent on Provincial or Municipal Governments. 
4. Private Stations. 

The first three categories are responsible directly 
or indirectly to the Central Authorities, transmitting ident- 
ical programmes in which Chinese politics and the education of 
the masses play the greater part. They are subsidised by 
the Central Government (Minister of Communications) and by the 


Prowincial Governments. 


SITUATION ON JANUARY 1, 1956. 
Up till December 1935 private radio broadcasting 


statione were not subject to the control of the Central Auth= 
orities. Provisional Regulations, which are still in force, 
governed them (See Appendix III). 

Since that time the Central Government has become 
very anxious regarding the great freedom accorded to private 
stations. Control bureaux have been set gp in the prin- 


cipal towns in Chine (Shanghai, Nanking, Tientsin, Peiping, 


Mankow, Canton, stc). These control bureaux have it as 

a duty to bring to the notice of the tiinister of Commun- 
ications all the faults of the stutions under their control. 
In accordance with Article <“<V of the Provisional Regu- 
lations, the Minister of Communications may cancel those 


licences issued to stations for infringements. 


In 1936 (November), a Broudcasting Central Commit- 
tee was created, the head office of which is sgituuteu in 
Nanking. New restrictions concerning private radio stat- 
ions were adopted. They tend to make Chinese broadcast- 
ing a means of cultural instruction (See Appendix IV - 
Time 3schedule for Rroadcasts from Private Radio Stations). 

The Central Government, however, is running counter 
to the irlerests or the owners of ».-rivate stations, for 
the hours set apart for the transmission of educational 
programmes obtain the greater part of their revenues. 

From 8 pom until 9.5 p.m for exanple, orivate stations 
must re-transmit the programmes broadcast by the central 
station in Nanking: now this hour is the most remuner- 


ative for the transmission of advertising announcements. 


REMARKS. 

Following the example of other powers, China is 
obviously attempting to bring its broadcasting syctem under 
state control. In Shanghai, in particular, a certain 
number of private stations will be closed down during 1937. 

A statute on Chinese rudio broadcasting is now 
in the procese of being prepared in Nanking. It will be 


promulgated in several months‘ time.
